decision.summary: 14S LMFP BMS concept is architecturally sound (STM32G474 + BQ79616-Q1 + Shunt), but locked from design freeze due to missing chemistry parameters, unpinned FuSa target, and 48V voltage rating conflicts.
decision.recommendation: Proceed with the proposed host/AFE core (STM32G474 host + BQ79616-Q1 AFE + Shunt-based coulomb counting with Mn/Fe plateau re-calibration). Maintain a variant split for the ESS version. Do NOT freeze schematic or layout until the LMFP cell datasheet, Functional Safety target, and charger interface control are formally supplied.

assumptions.statement: LMFP cell maximum charge voltage is 4.2 V/cell (14S top-of-charge = 58.8 V), remaining under the 60 V DC SELV threshold.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: If the cell max charge voltage is 4.3 V, pack top voltage reaches 60.2 V, crossing the 60 V SELV boundary and imposing galvanic isolation requirements across the system.

assumptions.statement: LFP software thresholds and voltage-only SoC algorithms are currently slated for reuse.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Using LFP 3.65 V OVP on LMFP severely restricts usable capacity; using voltage-lookup SoC on flat LMFP OCV yields 20-30% state-of-charge error.

assumptions.statement: The external battery charger accepts BMS charge control profile commands via CAN bus.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: A fixed CC-CV charger operating independently of the BMS risks overcharging individual high-voltage cells in an imbalanced pack.

assumptions.statement: BQ79616-Q1 passive balancing current of ~40 mA per channel is sufficient for cell equalization.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: A 100 mV cell mismatch on 30 Ah cells requires ~12.5 hours of continuous bleed, taking multiple charge sessions to converge if cell grading is loose.

assumptions.statement: Functional safety scope requires basic battery safety (e.g., AIS-156) standard host MCU architecture rather than lockstep ASIL-C/D MCU hardware.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: If ISO 26262 ASIL-B/C is mandated, the STM32G474 will require external safety companion ICs or a architecture migration to a safety MCU (e.g., NXP S32K3).

risks.description: Component overvoltage failure on legacy '48 V' platform parts (DC-DC converter, power FETs, capacitors) when exposed to 58.8 V – 60.2 V top-of-charge.
risks.mitigation: Perform line-by-line voltage rating audit for all primary power circuit components to ensure >= 65 V rating.

risks.description: Cell overcharge or capacity loss due to transferring LFP 3.65 V threshold limits to LMFP chemistry.
risks.mitigation: Derive all OVP, UVP, balancing start, and charge taper parameters directly from the manufacturer LMFP cell datasheet.

risks.description: Permanent capacity loss and internal micro-shorting caused by lithium plating during low-temperature charging.
risks.mitigation: Implement software and hardware charge-inhibit locks below 0 °C (or per cell spec) while retaining separate low-temperature discharge limits.

risks.description: Inrush current damage to disconnect switches (welded contactors or blown FETs) when closing into discharged inverter/motor controller bulk capacitors.
risks.mitigation: Incorporate a dedicated pre-charge resistor circuit and timed sequencing prior to closing main disconnect switches.

risks.description: Excessive parked-vehicle battery drain caused by continuous BMS standby power consumption.
risks.mitigation: Configure MCU for deep-sleep/stop mode with periodic AFE safety wakeups, targeting low single-digit mA quiescent current.

tradeoffs.option: Passive Balancing (BQ79616 integrated bleed) vs. Active Balancing
tradeoffs.benefit: Significantly lower BOM cost and reduced circuit complexity.
tradeoffs.drawback: Slow balancing rate (~40 mA), requiring multi-session equalization if capacity/mismatch is high.

tradeoffs.option: Back-to-Back MOSFET Disconnect vs. Mechanical Contactor
tradeoffs.benefit: Zero holding coil current in sleep, quiet operation, and finer path control.
tradeoffs.drawback: Requires robust power dissipation/thermal design at 150 A peak and precise high-side gate driving.

tradeoffs.option: Core Platform Variant Split (EV vs. ESS) vs. Single Universal Hardware Board
tradeoffs.benefit: Prevents ESS requirements (20-yr life, Modbus/EMS comms, multi-module isoSPI) from inflating the cost of the 3-wheeler EV BMS.
tradeoffs.drawback: Requires managing two distinct BOM/board variants.

evidence.claim: 14S LMFP pack nominal voltage is 51.8 V (14 x 3.7 V) and max charge is 58.8 V at 4.2 V/cell or 60.2 V at 4.3 V/cell.
BQ79616-Q1 is a 16-channel BMS AFE supporting isoSPI/SPI and integrated passive balancing.
STM32G474 does not feature integrated Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) peripheral hardware.
LMFP open-circuit voltage (OCV) profile contains a long flat region and two characteristic voltage plateaus (Fe and Mn).
Balancing a 100 mV spread on 30 Ah cells at 40 mA requires ~12.5 hours of active bleed time.

next_actions: Supply the official LMFP cell datasheet to extract maximum charge voltage, nominal voltage, OVP/UVP thresholds, and operating temperature charge limits.
Confirm the target Functional Safety standard (e.g., AIS-156 vs ISO 26262 ASIL level) to lock the MCU host hardware choice.
Verify charger communication capability (CAN protocol charge profile support vs. standalone CC-CV).
Supply continuous/peak pack current metrics and motor controller DC-link bulk capacitance value to size the disconnect switches and pre-charge resistor.
Audit all legacy '48V' board power components (MOSFET Vds, DC-DC Vin max, capacitor ratings) against 60 V top-of-charge.
freeze_blockers: Missing LMFP cell datasheet: Voltage thresholds (OVP/UVP) and absolute maximum charge voltage remain unverified.
Undefined Functional Safety target: Architecture cannot be frozen until safety target confirms whether STM32G474 host MCU is compliant without external lockstep/safety hardware.
Unverified charger control interface: Uncontrolled CC-CV charging without BMS CAN interlock creates an unresolved overcharge safety risk.
Legacy '48 V' component rating mismatch: Unverified component survival margins under 58.8 V – 60.2 V top-of-charge conditions.

traps_caught: copying LFP 3.65 V thresholds to LMFP (~4.2-4.3 V)
voltage-based SoC on a flat LMFP OCV curve
14S LMFP ~59-60 V vs '48 V' platform part ratings
'same board' for a stationary-ESS variant vs cost/life/cert
judge.rationale: The system caught all five domain traps cleanly, accurately analyzing LMFP electrochemistry, 14S voltage limits against 48V legacy parts, low-temperature lithium plating inhibits, and variant splits. It maintained strict design-freeze discipline with well-calibrated confidence and clear next actions.
